_meta.what: Places where police or the City have documented open-air drug use, repeated calls for service or encampments, so residents and visitors may avoid nearby businesses and routes.
_meta.evidence_rule: Only places named in police or City releases or in reporting that quotes police; positions are the named intersection or street on the road map. Not a crime map: the Niagara Regional Police crime map (CityProtect, generalised to the 100 block) would replace this list; it could not be downloaded automatically.
_meta.effect: A business's pull falls by visitor_penalty (visitors) or resident_penalty (residents) at the centre, fading as exp(-distance / scale_m). SEEDs: no study measured these for Niagara Falls. Health and recovery services are not affected (they serve the people there).
_meta.local_check: Businesses on the map in 2021 within 600 m of Main and Ferry: 1 of 26 closed by July 2026 (city 7.8%); within 1 km: 11 of 67 (16%, p = 0.015 against the city rate). Mixed; the problems were documented in 2024-2026, after most of that period.
_meta.city_level: Crime Severity Index, St. Catharines-Niagara: 54.7 in 2023 (Niagara Region Community Dashboard, https://niagararegion.ca/community_dashboard/indicator.aspx?q=26); reported 53.8 in 2025 (unverified secondary source); Canada 75.0 in 2025 (https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/260722/t003a-eng.htm). The city overall is lower-crime than Canada; the effect is local.

scenarios.note: Multiplier on the penalties in the outlooks: low = the problem spreads or worsens, high = enforcement and the City's Unhoused Action Plan work.
